plan.title: Paired within-subject DE: treated vs control blood samples
plan.analytical_narrative: Five subjects each contribute a control and a treated blood sample (paired design, raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 10 samples). The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — is answered by a paired differential expression test that models the subject as a blocking factor so that between-subject variability is removed and only the within-subject treatment effect is tested. Pipeline: (1) sample-structure QC on the raw counts to check that samples do not carry hidden batch structure or outliers, and to confirm subject pairing is visible in the data; (2) minimal low-count pre-filtering; (3) DESeq2 with design ~ subject + condition (condition releveled so 'control' is the reference), Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the condition coefficient, BH-adjusted at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering; (4) preranked fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome pathway gene sets (human, staged locally) using the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric, since the full ranked list captures coordinated sub-threshold signal that a short significant-gene list (likely given n=5 pairs) would miss; (5) an integrated report with fit diagnostics, the paired DE gene table (unshrunken and shrunken log2FC), and the pathway results, all with a full reproducibility record. This grounds directly in the Inflexa procedure for a paired 5-vs-5 human bulk RNA-seq design with STAR/featureCounts counts.

steps.method: vst(blind) PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size
keep genes with >=10 counts in >=5 samples (smallest group size)
design = ~subject + condition, explicit reference level = control
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
integrated report with diagnostics, DE table, enrichment results, reproducibility record
